source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

pt.L: E a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim:
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: an undated oracle: the day of the LORD on Egypt
decisions.reason: Verses 1-19 have no date. They describe the coming day of judgment on Egypt and its allies, city by city. Verses 20-26 are a separate, dated oracle.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, as in 1:3.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הִנָּבֵא֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֵילִ֖ילוּ הָ֥הּ לַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Wail, Alas for the day!

en.L: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Wail, "Alas for the day!"
en.B: Son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Wail and cry, "Alas for that day!"
en.R: Son of man, prophesy and say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Cry out in grief, "What a terrible day!"

pt.L: Filho do homem, profetiza e dize: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Lamentem: "Ai, que dia!"
pt.B: Filho do homem, profetiza e dize: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Gritem de dor e digam: "Ai daquele dia!"
pt.R: Filho do homem, profetiza e dize: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Chorem e gritem de tristeza: "Que dia terrível!"

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: Wail, Alas for the day!: a cry of grief at what is coming
decisions.reason: The LORD calls on Egypt to wail. "Alas" is a cry of pain; the day is the day of verse 3.

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B); Cry out in grief (R); Alas (L, B); What a terrible day (R)
decisions.reason: *Helilu* follows the Isaiah table. The cry Egypt is to raise is set in double quotes as the words people will say; Readable says what the cry of grief means.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Lamentem (L); Gritem de dor (B); Chorem e gritem de tristeza (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail takes the wording Isaiah 13:6 gives it in Portuguese at each level, plural, since the people of Egypt are called on; the cry itself is "Ai", the Portuguese cry of grief.

source.text: כִּֽי־קָר֣וֹב י֔וֹם וְקָר֥וֹב י֖וֹם לַֽיהוָ֑ה י֣וֹם עָנָ֔ן עֵ֥ת גּוֹיִ֖ם יִֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For near [is the] day, and near [is the] day of Yahweh; a day of cloud, a time of [the] nations it will be.

en.L: For the day [is] near, and the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] near; a day of cloud, a time of the nations it will be.
en.B: For the day is close; the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close. It will be a cloudy day, a time of reckoning for the nations.
en.R: The day is coming soon. The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is near. It will be a dark and cloudy day, a time when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will judge the nations.

pt.L: Pois perto [está] o dia, e perto [está] o dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; dia de nuvens, tempo das nações será.
pt.B: Pois o dia está perto; o dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está perto. Será um dia de nuvens, um tempo de acerto de contas para as nações.
pt.R: O dia está chegando. O dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está perto. Vai ser um dia escuro e cheio de nuvens, um tempo em que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vai julgar as nações.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD: the day the LORD acts in judgment
decisions.reason: See the note at Joel 1:15. The prophets speak of the day when the LORD comes to judge (Isaiah 13:6, 9; Zephaniah 1:7, 14). Here it falls on Egypt and its allies.

decisions.choice: a day of cloud, a time of the nations: a dark day of judgment for the nations
decisions.reason: Clouds and darkness go with the LORD's coming in judgment (Joel 2:2; Zephaniah 1:15). "A time of the nations" means their time has come.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD, at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps "the day of the LORD" at every level, as Isaiah 13:6. Balanced and Readable say what "a time of the nations" means (m2), and Readable names the LORD as the one who judges.

decisions.choice: o dia do SENHOR, at every level
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 13:6 in Portuguese: the name of the day stays at every level; Balanced and Readable say what "a time of the nations" means, as the English does.

source.text: וּבָאָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְהָיְתָ֤ה חַלְחָלָה֙ בְּכ֔וּשׁ בִּנְפֹ֥ל חָלָ֖ל בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְלָקְח֣וּ הֲמוֹנָ֔הּ וְנֶהֶרְס֖וּ יְסוֹדֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will come a sword on Egypt, and there will be anguish in Cush, when fall [the] slain in Egypt, and they take away its wealth, and torn down [are] its foundations.

en.L: And a sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will be in Cush, when the slain fall in Egypt, and they take away its abundance, and its foundations are torn down.
en.B: A sword will come against Egypt, and Cush will be in anguish when the slain fall in Egypt, when its wealth is carried off and its foundations are torn down.
en.R: War will come to Egypt, and the people of Cush will shake with fear. Many people in Egypt will be killed. Enemies will carry away Egypt's riches and tear down its foundations.

pt.L: E virá a espada sobre o Egito, e haverá angústia em Cuxe, quando caírem os mortos no Egito, e levarem a sua riqueza, e os seus alicerces forem derrubados.
pt.B: A espada virá contra o Egito, e Cuxe ficará angustiada quando os mortos caírem no Egito, quando a sua riqueza for levada e os seus alicerces forem derrubados.
pt.R: A guerra vai chegar ao Egito, e o povo de Cuxe vai tremer de medo. Muita gente no Egito vai ser morta. Os inimigos vão levar as riquezas do Egito e derrubar os seus alicerces.

decisions.choice: Cush: the land of the upper Nile, south of Egypt
decisions.reason: Cush (Nubia, in what is now Sudan) was Egypt's southern neighbor and at times its ruler. Its people would tremble at Egypt's fall (verse 9).

decisions.choice: its abundance: its wealth, or its crowds
decisions.reason: The word *hamon* (29:19) can mean Egypt's riches or its multitudes of people.

decisions.choice: War
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "sword".

source.text: כּ֣וּשׁ וּפ֤וּט וְלוּד֙ וְכָל־הָעֶ֣רֶב וְכ֔וּב וּבְנֵ֖י אֶ֣רֶץ הַבְּרִ֑ית אִתָּ֖ם בַּחֶ֥רֶב יִפֹּֽלוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Cush and Put and Lud and all the mixed people, and Kub, and [the] sons of [the] land of the covenant, with them by [the] sword will fall.

en.L: Cush and Put and Lud and all the mixed people, and Kub, and the {{gender:people|sons}} of the land of the covenant will fall with them by the sword.
en.B: Cush and Put and Lud, all the foreign peoples, Kub, and the people of the land in covenant with them will fall by the sword along with Egypt.
en.R: The people of Cush, Put, Lud and Kub, all the foreigners, and the people from the land that made a treaty with Egypt will be killed in war along with the Egyptians.

pt.L: Cuxe e Pute e Lude e toda a mistura de povos, e Cube, e os filhos da terra da aliança cairão com eles pela espada.
pt.B: Cuxe, Pute e Lude, todos os povos estrangeiros, Cube e o povo da terra aliada a eles cairão pela espada junto com o Egito.
pt.R: O povo de Cuxe, de Pute, de Lude e de Cube, todos os estrangeiros e o povo da terra que fez um tratado com o Egito vão ser mortos na guerra junto com os egípcios.

decisions.choice: Cush, Put and Lud: Egypt's allies and hired soldiers
decisions.reason: These peoples served in Egypt's armies (Jeremiah 46:9; Ezekiel 27:10). Put is usually placed in Libya; Lud may be Lydia or a people of Africa.

decisions.choice: all the mixed people: foreigners in Egypt's service
decisions.reason: The word means a mixed crowd of foreigners (Jeremiah 25:20; 50:37). Written with the same letters, it could also be "Arabia".

decisions.choice: Kub: an unknown people
decisions.reason: The name is found only here. With one letter changed it would be Lub, the Libyans, as the Greek translation reads (stated from general knowledge). The name is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: the sons of the land of the covenant: an allied people, or Judeans in Egypt
alternatives: the Judeans who had fled to Egypt
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean a people bound to Egypt by treaty, or the people of Judah who had fled to Egypt (Jeremiah 43-44), since "the covenant" usually means the LORD's covenant with Israel.

decisions.choice: people (L, gender default)
decisions.reason: The whole people is meant, so Literal takes the gender setting.

decisions.choice: os filhos da terra da aliança, with no gender setting
alternatives: o povo da terra da aliança
decisions.reason: "Filhos" already includes the whole people in Portuguese, as in 25:2, so Literal keeps the Hebrew word with no setting.

source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽפְלוּ֙ סֹמְכֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָרַ֖ד גְּא֣וֹן עֻזָּ֑הּ מִמִּגְדֹּ֣ל סְוֵנֵ֗ה בַּחֶ֨רֶב֙ יִפְּלוּ־בָ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: And will fall [those who] support Egypt, and will come down [the] pride of its strength; from Migdol [to] Syene by [the] sword they will fall in it, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Those who support Egypt will fall, and the pride of its strength will come down; from Migdol [to] Syene they will fall in it by the sword, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Those who hold Egypt up will fall, and its proud strength will come down. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within it, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: All who help Egypt will fall, and the strength Egypt is proud of will be gone. From Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, people will be killed in war, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Cairão os que sustentam o Egito, e descerá o orgulho da sua força; desde Migdol [até] Sevene cairão nele pela espada, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Os que apoiam o Egito cairão, e a sua força orgulhosa será abatida. Desde Migdol até Sevene cairão pela espada dentro dele, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Todos os que ajudam o Egito vão cair, e a força de que o Egito se orgulha vai acabar. Desde Migdol, no norte, até Assuã, no sul, as pessoas vão ser mortas na guerra, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: those who support Egypt: its allies and defenders
decisions.reason: The people of verse 5, and all who held Egypt up, fall with it.

decisions.choice: from Migdol to Syene: from one end of Egypt to the other
Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula with the divine name alone follows the Isaiah table.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

source.text: וְנָשַׁ֕מּוּ בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֑וֹת וְעָרָ֕יו בְּתוֹךְ־עָרִ֥ים נַחֲרָב֖וֹת תִּֽהְיֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will be desolate in [the] midst of lands made desolate, and its cities in [the] midst of cities laid waste will be.

en.L: And they will be desolate amid lands made desolate, and its cities will be amid cities laid waste.
en.B: They will be desolate among desolate lands, and its cities will lie among ruined cities.
en.R: Egypt will be an empty land among other empty lands. Its cities will lie in ruins among other ruined cities.

pt.L: E ficarão desolados no meio de terras desoladas, e as suas cidades estarão no meio de cidades arruinadas.
pt.B: Ficarão desolados entre terras desoladas, e as suas cidades ficarão entre cidades arruinadas.
pt.R: O Egito vai ser uma terra vazia entre outras terras vazias. As suas cidades vão ficar em ruínas entre outras cidades arruinadas.

decisions.choice: the words of 29:12
decisions.reason: The verse repeats what was said of Egypt in 29:12.

source.text: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּתִתִּי־אֵ֣שׁ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְנִשְׁבְּר֖וּ כָּל־עֹזְרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I put fire in Egypt, and are broken all its helpers.

en.L: And they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I put fire in Egypt, and all who help it are broken.
en.B: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I kindle a fire in Egypt and all its helpers are crushed.
en.R: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I start a fire in Egypt and destroy all who help it.

pt.L: E saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu puser fogo no Egito, e todos os que o ajudam forem quebrados.
pt.B: Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu acender fogo no Egito e todos os seus ajudantes forem esmagados.
pt.R: Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu puser fogo no Egito e destruir todos os que o ajudam.

decisions.choice: when I set fire to Egypt: when war and destruction come on it
decisions.reason: Fire is the burning of cities in war (verses 14, 16).

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יֵצְא֨וּ מַלְאָכִ֤ים מִלְּפָנַי֙ בַּצִּ֔ים לְהַחֲרִ֖יד אֶת־כּ֣וּשׁ בֶּ֑טַח וְהָיְתָ֨ה חַלְחָלָ֤ה בָהֶם֙ בְּי֣וֹם מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י הִנֵּ֖ה בָּאָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: On that day will go out messengers from before me in ships to terrify Cush [in its] security; and there will be anguish on them on [the] day of Egypt, for look, it is coming.

en.L: In that day messengers will go forth from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence in ships to terrify Cush [in its] security, and anguish will be upon them on the day of Egypt; for look, it is coming.
en.B: On that day messengers will set out from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in ships to terrify Cush, which feels secure. Anguish will seize them on the day of Egypt's doom, for it is surely coming.
en.R: At that time I will send messengers in ships to frighten the people of Cush, who feel safe. They will be terrified on the day Egypt falls. And that day is coming!

pt.L: Naquele dia sairão mensageiros de diante de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} em navios para aterrorizar Cuxe [na sua] segurança, e haverá angústia sobre eles no dia do Egito; pois eis que vem.
pt.B: Naquele dia sairão mensageiros da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} parte em navios para aterrorizar Cuxe, que se sente segura. A angústia tomará conta deles no dia da ruína do Egito, pois ele certamente vem.
pt.R: Naquele tempo vou mandar mensageiros em navios para assustar o povo de Cuxe, que se sente seguro. Eles vão ficar apavorados no dia em que o Egito cair. E esse dia está chegando!

decisions.choice: messengers in ships to Cush: an echo of Isaiah 18:2
decisions.reason: Isaiah 18:2 speaks of Cush sending envoys in boats on the Nile. Now messengers go up the river to Cush with the news of Egypt's fall.

decisions.choice: the day of Egypt: the day of Egypt's judgment
decisions.reason: As "the day of Jerusalem" in Psalm 137:7, the day of a city or land is the day of its fall.

decisions.choice: In that day (L); On that day (B); At that time (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *bayyom hahu*.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ אֶת־הֲמ֣וֹן מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּיַ֖ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶלֶךְ־בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I will put an end to [the] abundance of Egypt by [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I will put an end to the abundance of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: By the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon I will bring the hordes of Egypt to an end.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will use Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon to put an end to Egypt's great crowds of people.

pt.L: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Farei cessar a multidão do Egito pela mão de Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia.
pt.B: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Pela mão de Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, porei fim às multidões do Egito.
pt.R: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Vou usar Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, para acabar com as grandes multidões do Egito.

decisions.choice: the abundance of Egypt: its crowds and wealth
decisions.reason: The word *hamon* (29:19) here means Egypt's teeming people and its pomp.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Ezekiel spells the name with an r (see 26:7).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: a multidão (L); as multidões (B); as grandes multidões (R)
decisions.reason: For hamon in chapters 29-32: Portuguese "multidão" holds the crowds and the bustle of a great land (m1); "riqueza" is used where the English says "wealth" or "abundance" of goods (29:19; 30:4).

source.text: ה֠וּא וְעַמּ֤וֹ אִתּוֹ֙ עָרִיצֵ֣י גוֹיִ֔ם מֽוּבָאִ֖ים לְשַׁחֵ֣ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהֵרִ֤יקוּ חַרְבוֹתָם֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמָלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ חָלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: He and his people with him, [the] most ruthless of [the] nations, will be brought in to destroy the land; and they will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land [with the] slain.

en.L: He, and his people with him, the ruthless of the nations, are being brought to ruin the land; and they will unsheathe their swords against Egypt and fill the land [with] slain.
en.B: He and his army with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to ruin the land. They will bare their swords against Egypt and fill the land with corpses.
en.R: He and his army, the cruelest army of all, will come to ruin the land. They will pull out their swords to attack Egypt and fill the land with dead bodies.

pt.L: Ele, e o seu povo com ele, os mais cruéis das nações, são trazidos para arruinar a terra; e desembainharão as suas espadas contra o Egito e encherão a terra de mortos.
pt.B: Ele e o seu exército com ele, a mais cruel das nações, serão trazidos para arruinar a terra. Desembainharão as espadas contra o Egito e encherão a terra de cadáveres.
pt.R: Ele e o seu exército, o exército mais cruel de todos, vão vir para arruinar a terra. Vão puxar as espadas para atacar o Egito e encher a terra de corpos.

decisions.choice: the most ruthless of the nations: Babylon

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֤י יְאֹרִים֙ חָֽרָבָ֔ה וּמָכַרְתִּ֥י אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיַד־רָעִ֑ים וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִ֞י אֶ֤רֶץ וּמְלֹאָהּ֙ בְּיַד־זָרִ֔ים אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make [the] streams dry ground, and I will sell the land into [the] hand of evil [men], and I will make desolate [the] land and its fullness by [the] hand of strangers; I, Yahweh, have spoken.

en.L: And I will make the streams dry ground, and I will sell the land into the hand of evildoers; and I will make desolate the land and all that fills it by the hand of strangers; I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.B: I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land into the power of evil men. By the hand of foreigners I will lay waste the land and everything in it. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.R: I will dry up the streams of the Nile. I will hand the land over to evil people. I will use foreigners to destroy the land and everything in it. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have said it.

pt.L: E farei dos rios terra seca, e venderei a terra na mão de malfeitores; e assolarei a terra e tudo o que a enche pela mão de estrangeiros; eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, falei.
pt.B: Secarei os braços do Nilo e venderei a terra ao poder de homens maus. Pela mão de estrangeiros devastarei a terra e tudo o que há nela. Eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, falei.
pt.R: Vou secar os braços do Nilo. Vou entregar a terra a gente má. Vou usar estrangeiros para destruir a terra e tudo o que há nela. Eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, disse isso.

decisions.choice: the streams made dry: Egypt's life taken away
decisions.reason: Egypt depended entirely on the Nile and its channels (29:3). To dry them is to end its life (Isaiah 19:5-7).

decisions.choice: sell the land into the hand of evil men: hand it over to them
decisions.reason: To "sell" into someone's hand is to give into their power (Judges 2:14; 4:2).

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, have spoken (L, B); have said it (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording, as in 5:13 and 17:24.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֨י גִלּוּלִ֜ים וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֤י אֱלִילִים֙ מִנֹּ֔ף וְנָשִׂ֥יא מֵאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ע֑וֹד וְנָתַתִּ֥י יִרְאָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I will destroy [the] idols and put an end to [the] worthless gods from Memphis, and a prince from [the] land of Egypt there will not be again; and I will put fear in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I will destroy the filthy idols and put an end to the worthless gods from Memphis, and there will no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt; and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the worthless gods in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince in the land of Egypt, and I will fill the land of Egypt with fear.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will wipe out the idols and get rid of the useless gods in Memphis. Egypt will no longer have a ruler of its own. I will fill the land of Egypt with fear.

pt.L: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Destruirei os ídolos imundos e farei cessar os deuses inúteis de Mênfis, e não haverá mais príncipe da terra do Egito; e porei temor na terra do Egito.
pt.B: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Destruirei os ídolos e porei fim aos deuses inúteis de Mênfis. Não haverá mais príncipe na terra do Egito, e encherei de medo a terra do Egito.
pt.R: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Vou acabar com os ídolos e me livrar dos deuses que não servem para nada em Mênfis. O Egito não vai mais ter um governante seu. Vou encher de medo a terra do Egito.

decisions.choice: idols ... worthless gods
decisions.reason: The first word is *gillulim*, Ezekiel's word of contempt for idols (see 6:4). The second, *elilim*, means "nothings", gods that are worthless (Isaiah 2:8; Psalm 96:5).

decisions.choice: Memphis: the old capital of Lower Egypt
decisions.reason: Memphis, near modern Cairo, was a great city with famous temples (Hosea 9:6; Jeremiah 46:14). The Hebrew calls it Noph.

decisions.choice: no prince from the land of Egypt: no native ruler
decisions.reason: Egypt would be ruled by foreigners. For most of its later history it was (29:15).

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim*; see 6:4. *Elilim* is "worthless gods" at Literal and Balanced and "useless gods" at Readable. *Nasi'* is "prince" (L, B) and "ruler" (R).

decisions.choice: ídolos imundos (L), ídolos (B, R); deuses inúteis (L, B); Mênfis
decisions.reason: Gillulim takes the wording 14:3 sets for the book; elilim is "deuses inúteis", gods that are nothing. Noph is "Mênfis" at every level, as Isaiah 19:13 and Jeremiah 46:14 have it in Portuguese.

source.text: וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִי֙ אֶת־פַּתְר֔וֹס וְנָתַ֥תִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּצֹ֑עַן וְעָשִׂ֥יתִי שְׁפָטִ֖ים בְּנֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make desolate Pathros, and I will put fire in Zoan, and I will execute judgments on Thebes.

en.L: And I will make Pathros desolate, and I will set fire to Zoan, and I will execute judgments on Thebes.
en.B: I will lay Pathros waste, set fire to Zoan and carry out judgments on Thebes.
en.R: I will destroy southern Egypt, set fire to the city of Zoan and punish the city of Thebes.

pt.L: E assolarei Patros, e porei fogo em Zoã, e executarei juízos em Tebas.
pt.B: Devastarei Patros, porei fogo em Zoã e executarei juízos sobre Tebas.
pt.R: Vou destruir o sul do Egito, pôr fogo na cidade de Zoã e castigar a cidade de Tebas.

decisions.choice: Pathros, Zoan and Thebes: the south, a city of the delta, and the great southern capital
decisions.reason: Pathros is Upper Egypt (29:14). Zoan (Tanis) was a royal city in the northeast delta (Isaiah 19:11). Thebes, called No in Hebrew, was the great city of the god Amon in the south (Jeremiah 46:25; Nahum 3:8). Verses 13-18 move up and down the land, naming its chief cities.

decisions.choice: Thebes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name No is given its familiar Greek name, Thebes, at every level, as Jeremiah 46:25 does. Readable says "southern Egypt" for Pathros, as at 29:14.

decisions.choice: Zoã; Tebas
decisions.reason: Zoan in the form Isaiah 19:13 gives it, and No as "Tebas" at every level, as Jeremiah 46:25 has it.

source.text: וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֣י חֲמָתִ֔י עַל־סִ֖ין מָע֣וֹז מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י אֶת־הֲמ֥וֹן נֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will pour out my wrath on Sin, [the] stronghold of Egypt, and I will cut off [the] abundance of Thebes.

en.L: And I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on Sin, the stronghold of Egypt, and I will cut off the abundance of Thebes.
en.B: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on Sin, the fortress of Egypt, and cut off the hordes of Thebes.
en.R: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on Pelusium, Egypt's fortress, and I will kill the crowds of people in Thebes.

pt.L: E derramarei o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor sobre Sim, a fortaleza do Egito, e eliminarei a multidão de Tebas.
pt.B: Derramarei o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor sobre Sim, a fortaleza do Egito, e eliminarei as multidões de Tebas.
pt.R: Vou derramar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira sobre Pelúsio, a fortaleza do Egito, e vou matar as multidões de Tebas.

decisions.choice: Sin, the stronghold of Egypt: Pelusium on the northeastern border
decisions.reason: Sin is usually identified with Pelusium, the fortress that guarded Egypt's border toward Sinai and the road from Canaan (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: wrath (L, B); anger (R); Sin (L, B); Pelusium (R)
decisions.reason: *Chemah* follows the settled wording. Readable gives Sin its better-known name.

source.text: וְנָתַ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם ח֤וּל תָּחוּל֙ סִ֔ין וְנֹ֖א תִּהְיֶ֣ה לְהִבָּקֵ֑עַ וְנֹ֖ף צָרֵ֥י יוֹמָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will put fire in Egypt; Sin will writhe greatly, and Thebes will be broken open, and Memphis [will have] foes by day.

en.L: And I will set fire to Egypt; Sin will writhe in anguish, and Thebes will be broken open, and Memphis [will face] foes by day.
en.B: I will set fire to Egypt. Sin will writhe in agony, Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face enemies in broad daylight.
en.R: I will set Egypt on fire. Pelusium will be in great pain. Enemies will break through the walls of Thebes. They will attack Memphis in broad daylight.

pt.L: E porei fogo no Egito; Sim se contorcerá de angústia, e Tebas será arrombada, e Mênfis [enfrentará] inimigos em pleno dia.
pt.B: Porei fogo no Egito. Sim se contorcerá de dor, Tebas terá os seus muros rompidos, e Mênfis enfrentará inimigos em plena luz do dia.
pt.R: Vou pôr fogo no Egito. Pelúsio vai sentir uma dor terrível. Os inimigos vão romper os muros de Tebas. Vão atacar Mênfis em plena luz do dia.

decisions.choice: Memphis [will face] foes by day
alternatives: and the waters of Memphis will burst out
decisions.reason: The words are hard: "and Noph (Memphis), enemies by day". They seem to mean that Memphis will be attacked openly, in daylight. Small changes to the text have been suggested, such as "its walls will be breached", but none is certain.

decisions.choice: Sin will writhe greatly: the verb is doubled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis: Sin will writhe as a woman in labor.

source.text: בַּח֥וּרֵי אָ֛וֶן וּפִי־בֶ֖סֶת בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֑לוּ וְהֵ֖נָּה בַּשְּׁבִ֥י תֵלַֽכְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] young men of Aven and Pi-beseth by [the] sword will fall, and they [the women] into captivity will go.

en.L: The young men of Aven and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and they [the cities] will go into captivity.
en.B: The young men of Aven and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and the cities themselves will go into captivity.
en.R: The young men of the cities of On and Pi-beseth will be killed in war. And the people of those cities will be taken away as captives.

pt.L: Os jovens de Áven e de Pi-Besete cairão pela espada, e elas [as cidades] irão para o cativeiro.
pt.B: Os jovens de Áven e de Pi-Besete cairão pela espada, e as próprias cidades irão para o cativeiro.
pt.R: Os jovens das cidades de Om e de Pi-Besete vão ser mortos na guerra. E o povo dessas cidades vai ser levado como prisioneiro.

decisions.choice: Aven and Pi-beseth: On (Heliopolis) and Bubastis in the delta
decisions.reason: Aven is the city of On (Genesis 41:45), the center of sun worship later called Heliopolis. The vowels turn "On" into *aven*, "wickedness", the same play as "Beth-aven" for Bethel (Hosea 4:15). Pi-beseth is Bubastis, a city of the cat goddess Bastet, in the eastern delta (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: and they will go into captivity: "they" is feminine, the cities or their women
alternatives: and the women will go into captivity
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine. It may mean the cities, spoken of as women, or the women of those cities.

decisions.choice: On (R); Aven (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew form and its play on words, with a footnote (m1); Readable gives the city's name.

decisions.choice: Áven (L, B); Om (R); Pi-Besete
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew form and its play on "wickedness" (m1); Readable gives the city's name as Genesis 41:45 has it in Portuguese, "Om".

source.text: וּבִֽתְחַפְנְחֵס֙ חָשַׂ֣ךְ הַיּ֔וֹם בְּשִׁבְרִי־שָׁם֙ אֶת־מֹט֣וֹת מִצְרַ֔יִם וְנִשְׁבַּת־בָּ֖הּ גְּא֣וֹן עֻזָּ֑הּ הִ֚יא עָנָ֣ן יְכַסֶּ֔נָּה וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ בַּשְּׁבִ֥י תֵלַֽכְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And in Tahpanhes the day will withhold [its light], when I break there [the] yoke bars of Egypt, and will cease in it [the] pride of its strength; it, a cloud will cover it, and its daughters into captivity will go.

en.L: And in Tahpanhes the day will grow dark, when I break there the yoke bars of Egypt, and the pride of its strength will cease in it; as for it, a cloud will cover it, and its daughters will go into captivity.
en.B: At Tahpanhes the day will turn dark when I break Egypt's yoke bars there, and its proud strength will come to an end. A cloud will cover it, and its daughter towns will go into captivity.
en.R: At Tahpanhes the daylight will turn to darkness when I break the power Egypt held over others. Its proud strength will come to an end. A cloud will cover the city, and the people of its villages will be taken away as captives.

pt.L: E em Tafnes o dia escurecerá, quando eu quebrar ali as cangas do Egito, e cessar nela o orgulho da sua força; quanto a ela, uma nuvem a cobrirá, e as suas filhas irão para o cativeiro.
pt.B: Em Tafnes o dia ficará escuro quando eu quebrar ali as cangas do Egito, e a sua força orgulhosa chegará ao fim. Uma nuvem a cobrirá, e as cidades que dependem dela irão para o cativeiro.
pt.R: Em Tafnes a luz do dia vai virar escuridão quando eu quebrar o poder que o Egito tinha sobre os outros. A sua força orgulhosa vai acabar. Uma nuvem vai cobrir a cidade, e o povo das suas aldeias vai ser levado como prisioneiro.

decisions.choice: Tahpanhes: a border fortress in the eastern delta
decisions.reason: Jeremiah and the Judeans who fled after Jerusalem's fall settled there (Jeremiah 43:7-9). The Hebrew spells it here Tehaphnehes.

decisions.choice: the day will grow dark
decisions.reason: The standard text reads "the day will withhold (its light)". Many Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "will be dark", which differs by one letter (stated from general knowledge). Both give the same sense.

decisions.choice: the yoke bars of Egypt: the power by which Egypt held others
decisions.reason: A yoke bar held an animal or a people in subjection (34:27; Leviticus 26:13). Breaking Egypt's yoke ends its rule. With other vowels the word means "scepters".

decisions.choice: daughter towns (B); the people of its villages (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "daughters" means (26:6).

decisions.choice: Tafnes
decisions.reason: The town takes the form Jeremiah 43:7 and 44:1 give it in Portuguese, though the Hebrew here spells it a little differently (m1).

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתִי שְׁפָטִ֖ים בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So I will carry out judgments on Egypt. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will punish Egypt. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E executarei juízos no Egito, e saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Assim executarei juízos sobre o Egito. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Vou castigar o Egito. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: judgments: punishments carried out as sentences
and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בָּֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] eleventh year, in the first [month], on [the] seventh of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: And it came about in the eleventh year, in the first [month], on the seventh of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: In the first month of the eleventh year, on its seventh day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: On the seventh day of the first month, in the eleventh year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

pt.L: E aconteceu no décimo primeiro ano, no primeiro [mês], no sétimo [dia] do mês, [que] a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: No primeiro mês do décimo primeiro ano, no sétimo dia, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim:
pt.R: No sétimo dia do primeiro mês, no décimo primeiro ano do nosso exílio, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: the eleventh year, the first month, the seventh day: April 587 BC
decisions.reason: Counted from Jehoiachin's exile, the date falls in April 587 BC (stated from general knowledge), about three months after 29:1 and some months before Jerusalem fell.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֶת־זְר֛וֹעַ פַּרְעֹ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם שָׁבָ֑רְתִּי וְהִנֵּ֣ה לֹֽא־חֻ֠בְּשָׁה לָתֵ֨ת רְפֻא֜וֹת לָשׂ֥וּם חִתּ֛וּל לְחָבְשָׁ֥הּ לְחָזְקָ֖הּ לִתְפֹּ֥שׂ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt I have broken, and look, it has not been bound up to give healing, to put a bandage to bind it, to make it strong to grasp the sword.

en.L: Son of man, the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt I have broken, and look, it has not been bound up, to apply remedies, to put on a bandage to bind it up, so that it may become strong to grasp the sword.
en.B: Son of man, I have broken the arm of Egypt's king, Pharaoh. It has not been bandaged for healing or put in a splint to make it strong enough to hold a sword.
en.R: Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. No one has bandaged it so that it can heal. It has not been tied up to make it strong enough to hold a sword again.

pt.L: Filho do homem, o braço de Faraó, rei do Egito, eu quebrei, e eis que não foi enfaixado para lhe aplicar remédios, para lhe pôr uma atadura que o prenda, para que fique forte para segurar a espada.
pt.B: Filho do homem, eu quebrei o braço do rei do Egito, Faraó. Ele não foi enfaixado para sarar nem posto numa tala para ficar forte e segurar a espada.
pt.R: Filho do homem, eu quebrei o braço de Faraó, o rei do Egito. Ninguém o enfaixou para que ele sarasse. Ninguém o amarrou para que ficasse forte e pudesse segurar a espada outra vez.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: I have broken the arm of Pharaoh: Egypt's defeat as it tried to help Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength in war. Pharaoh Hophra's army came out to relieve Jerusalem and was driven back by the Babylonians (Jeremiah 37:5-11), not long before this date.

decisions.choice: a bandage to bind it: a splint or binding for a broken bone
decisions.reason: The words describe the setting of a broken arm, which is not done; Egypt will not recover its strength.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה הִנְנִי֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְשָֽׁבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־זְרֹ֣עֹתָ֔יו אֶת־הַחֲזָקָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַנִּשְׁבָּ֑רֶת וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥י אֶת־הַחֶ֖רֶב מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms, the strong and the broken, and I will make fall the sword from his hand.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms, the strong one and the broken one, and I will make the sword fall from his hand.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the one already broken, and make the sword fall from his hand.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am against Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the good one and the one that is already broken. I will make his sword fall out of his hand.

pt.L: Por isso, assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Eis que eu [estou] contra Faraó, rei do Egito, e quebrarei os seus braços, o forte e o quebrado, e farei cair a espada da sua mão.
pt.B: Por isso, assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Estou contra Faraó, rei do Egito. Quebrarei os seus dois braços, o forte e o que já está quebrado, e farei a espada cair da sua mão.
pt.R: Por isso, é isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Estou contra Faraó, o rei do Egito. Vou quebrar os dois braços dele, o bom e o que já está quebrado. Vou fazer a espada cair da mão dele.

decisions.choice: both his arms, the strong and the broken: all Egypt's strength
decisions.reason: The one arm is already broken (verse 21); now the other, still strong, will be broken too. Egypt will have no power left to fight.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks.

source.text: וַהֲפִצוֹתִ֥י אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וְזֵרִיתִ֖ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will scatter Egypt among [the] nations and disperse them among [the] lands.

en.L: And I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands.
en.B: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them through the lands.
en.R: I will scatter the people of Egypt among the nations and send them off to other countries.

pt.L: E espalharei o Egito entre as nações e os dispersarei pelas terras.
pt.B: Espalharei os egípcios entre as nações e os dispersarei pelas terras.
pt.R: Vou espalhar o povo do Egito entre as nações e mandá-lo para outros países.

decisions.choice: the words of 29:12
decisions.reason: The sentence repeats 29:12 and returns in verse 26.

source.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֗י אֶת־זְרֹעוֹת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־חַרְבִּ֖י בְּיָד֑וֹ וְשָׁבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־זְרֹע֣וֹת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְנָאַ֛ק נַאֲק֥וֹת חָלָ֖ל לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will strengthen [the] arms of [the] king of Babylon, and I will put my sword in his hand; and I will break [the] arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan [the] groans of a mortally wounded [man] before him.

en.L: And I will make strong the arms of the king of Babylon, and I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword in his hand; and the arms of Pharaoh I will break, and he will groan before him with the groans of a mortally wounded man.
en.B: I will give strength to the arms of the king of Babylon and place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword in his hand. But Pharaoh's arms I will break, and he will groan before him like a man mortally wounded.
en.R: I will make the king of Babylon strong and give him {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword to hold. But Pharaoh's arms I will break. He will groan in front of the king of Babylon like a man who is dying from his wounds.

pt.L: E fortalecerei os braços do rei da Babilônia e porei a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada na sua mão; e os braços de Faraó quebrarei, e ele gemerá diante dele com os gemidos de um ferido de morte.
pt.B: Darei força aos braços do rei da Babilônia e colocarei a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada na sua mão. Mas os braços de Faraó eu quebrarei, e ele gemerá diante dele como um homem ferido de morte.
pt.R: Vou tornar forte o rei da Babilônia e dar a ele a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada para segurar. Mas os braços de Faraó eu vou quebrar. Ele vai gemer diante do rei da Babilônia como um homem que está morrendo por causa dos ferimentos.

decisions.choice: my sword in his hand: Babylon fights as the LORD's agent
decisions.reason: The sword is the LORD's; the king of Babylon only carries it (21:8-22; 29:20).

decisions.choice: before him: before the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Pharaoh groans in front of his conqueror.

source.text: וְהַחֲזַקְתִּ֗י אֶת־זְרֹעוֹת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וּזְרֹע֥וֹת פַּרְעֹ֖ה תִּפֹּ֑לְנָה וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּתִתִּ֤י חַרְבִּי֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְנָטָ֥ה אוֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will strengthen [the] arms of [the] king of Babylon, and [the] arms of Pharaoh will fall; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I put my sword into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he stretches it out against [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword into the hand of Babylon's king, and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.
en.B: I will make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh's arms will drop. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I hand {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword to the king of Babylon and he swings it against the land of Egypt.
en.R: I will make the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh will become weak. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he uses it against the land of Egypt.

pt.L: E fortalecerei os braços do rei da Babilônia, mas os braços de Faraó cairão; e saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu der a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada na mão do rei da Babilônia, e ele a estender contra a terra do Egito.
pt.B: Tornarei fortes os braços do rei da Babilônia, mas os braços de Faraó cairão sem força. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu entregar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada ao rei da Babilônia e ele a brandir contra a terra do Egito.
pt.R: Vou tornar forte o rei da Babilônia, mas Faraó vai ficar fraco. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, quando eu puser a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada na mão do rei da Babilônia e ele a usar contra a terra do Egito.

decisions.choice: the arms of Pharaoh will fall: his strength will fail
decisions.reason: Arms that fall or hang down are arms with no strength left (Ezekiel 7:17).

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

source.text: וַהֲפִצוֹתִ֤י אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְזֵרִיתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will scatter Egypt among [the] nations and disperse them among [the] lands; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them through the lands. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will scatter the people of Egypt among the nations and send them off to other countries. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E espalharei o Egito entre as nações e os dispersarei pelas terras; e saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Espalharei os egípcios entre as nações e os dispersarei pelas terras. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Vou espalhar o povo do Egito entre as nações e mandá-lo para outros países. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the words of verse 23 again
decisions.reason: The oracle ends by repeating verse 23 and adding the refrain.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.
